usageNotes: Use this to create a cluster-wide logical PCI device mapping that can be referenced in VM configurations instead of hard-coding physical addresses. The `map` array must list per-node entries in `node=<name>,path=<DDDD:BB:SS.F>,id=<vendor:device>` format so Proxmox can resolve the correct physical device on each node at VM start time. Requires the `Mapping.Modify` privilege on `/mapping/pci`; returns null on success (no UPID — operation is synchronous).

examples.summary: Create a logical PCI mapping for a GPU present on two cluster nodes

params.description: NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU — available on pve1 and pve2

tips: The `id` field must follow the pve-configid format: lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens, no spaces.
Each entry in `map` is a comma-separated key=value string: node, path (PCI address in DDDD:BB:SS.F notation), and id (vendor:device hex).
Set `mdev: true` only for devices that expose mediated device (vGPU) interfaces; setting it on a bare-passthrough device has no effect.
`live-migration-capable` is experimental — only set it when both hardware IOMMU ACS and the guest driver explicitly support peer-to-peer DMA migration.
After creating a mapping here, reference it in a VM config via `hostpci0: mapping=<id>` rather than a raw PCI address.
